title: Count Number of Distinct Integers After Reverse Operations
summary: Given an array nums consisting of positive integers, reverse each integer, add the reversed integer to the end of the array, and return the count of distinct integers in the resulting array.
statement: Given an array nums consisting of positive integers, reverse each integer, add the reversed integer to the end of the array, and return the count of distinct integers in the resulting array.
constraints: For every original positive integer, reverse its decimal digits and append that numeric value conceptually.
Leading zeroes disappear when the reversal is interpreted as an integer.
Return the number of distinct original and reversed values.
hints: Insert every original value into a set.
Reverse each value’s decimal text, convert it back to an integer, and insert it.
A set removes duplicates across both the original and generated values, exactly matching the requested distinct count.
editorial: A set removes duplicates across both the original and generated values, exactly matching the requested distinct count.

tests.explanation: The combined distinct values are 1, 13, 10, 12, 31, and 21, giving six.
Reversing 100 produces 1, already present, and reversing 1 stays 1, so there are two distinct values.
